def snap_zero_point_to_uint8(rmin, rmax, qmin: int = 0, qmax: int = 255, min_real_range: float | None = None):
    """Snaps a uint8 activation zero-point to a canonical value based on the sign of the calibrated minimum.

    Some hardware targets require activation zero-points to take specific canonical values. This function
    snaps the zero-point of an (asymmetric) uint8 activation to one of two canonical values:

    * When ``rmin >= 0`` (activations are all non-negative), the zero-point is snapped to ``qmin`` (e.g. 0).
    * When ``rmin < 0`` (activations span negative values), the zero-point is snapped to the midpoint
      ``(qmin + qmax + 1) // 2`` (e.g. 128 for standard uint8 [0, 255]).

    The scale is recomputed so that the dequantized range still covers ``[rmin, rmax]`` without clipping,
    given the snapped (fixed) zero-point.

    :parameter rmin: minimum value of the calibrated real range.
    :parameter rmax: maximum value of the calibrated real range.
    :parameter qmin: minimum value representable by the target quantization data type. Defaults to 0.
    :parameter qmax: maximum value representable by the target quantization data type. Defaults to 255.
    :parameter min_real_range: Minimum floating-point range (i.e., rmax - rmin) to enforce. Defaults to None.
    :return: a tuple ``(zero_point, scale)`` where ``zero_point`` is a numpy uint8 scalar array and
        ``scale`` is a numpy float32 scalar array.
